verdict.rationale: Floot's docs say apps can include "jobs that run on a schedule, without a server to keep alive," which provides a basic mechanism for background automation. That is a single thin mention, with no detail on how users set up these automations, what triggers are available beyond scheduling, or any autonomous agent-driven background work. Missing for 10: documentation on configuring scheduled jobs, event- or webhook-based triggers, autonomous agent tasks that run without the user present, monitoring or retry behavior for background runs, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
